subject: OmniHealth SLA: request for buyout / fee-at-risk / LDs
messages:
From: Alicia Brewer <alicia.brewer@omnihealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: kent.hollis@omnihealth.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: OmniHealth SLA: request for buyout / fee-at-risk / LDs

Hi Neha / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the contract with procurement and legal and there are three points that are deal-breakers for us unless addressed in the SOW:

- Fee-at-risk / buyout: we need a clause that places up to 20% of the monthly committed fee at risk for repeated SLO misses (we'd prefer those funds escrowed).
- Termination right: if Redwood misses the 99.9% uptime SLO for two consecutive billing months, OmniHealth must have a unilateral right to terminate for convenience with a pro-rated buyout equal to remaining committed fees less accrued credits.
- Liquidated damages (LDs): in the event of data-integrity incidents tied to serving infrastructure (not user error), we need an LDs provision (capped) in addition to service credits—credits alone are insufficient for our regulatory posture.

I've attached a redline to the SLA (OmniHealth - Redwood SLA redline v2.pdf) with our suggested language. We're on a tight procurement timeline—aiming to sign by 6/3—so please let me know if Redwood can accept these points or what counterproposal you have.

Appreciate quick transparency so we can decide whether to push this to our board.

Best,
Alicia Brewer
VP, IT & Cloud Operations
OmniHealth

Alicia — thanks for the clear redline and timeline. We understand the urgency. I’m looping in Rishi (legal) and Marissa (AM) to review the exact language.

High-level, Redwood’s standard position is: credits tied to SLOs + documented remediation and escalation paths; we avoid uncapped buyouts and traditional LDs because they can be duplicative of credits and make forecasting impossible. That said, we’ve accepted limited fee-at-risk structures on strategic, committed deals before with clear caps and cure periods.

Can you confirm: 1) whether the requested 20% is of committed monthly fees or annual committed value, and 2) whether OmniHealth wants funds escrowed at signing or held as a contingent buyout? That will help speed Rishi’s review.

I’ll aim to get a counterproposal by end of day tomorrow. If it helps, can we do a 30-minute call for alignment?

Thanks — Neha

Subject: Fwd: OmniHealth SLA: request for buyout / fee-at-risk / LDs

Folks — quick legal read and suggested negotiation posture below. FYI I pulled examples from prior deals for reference.

Quoted for context:
> On Sat, 22 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700 Alicia wrote:
> > we need a clause that places up to 20% of the monthly committed fee at risk...
> > if Redwood misses the 99.9% uptime SLO for two consecutive billing months, OmniHealth must have a unilateral right to terminate for convenience with a pro-rated buyout equal to remaining committed fees less accrued credits.

Analysis / recommended approach:
1) Fee-at-risk: accept a fee-at-risk construct but cap at 10% of monthly committed fees and timebox to the first 6 months post-go-live or tied to a committed throughput milestone. We should refuse escrow of cash — instead, use a retention/holdback mechanism applied to quarterly invoices or an escrow capped at the reduced percent.
2) Termination right: reject unilateral immediate termination for convenience tied to two months of SLO misses. Propose staged remediation: an incident review + 30-day cure; if remediation fails and the customer experiences material repeated SLO misses beyond cure period, allow termination with a buyout equal to 3 months of committed fees (not full remaining term).
3) LDs: we can accept a narrowly scoped LDs provision for demonstrable, Redwood-caused data-integrity events, but cap aggregate LDs at the committed annual fee and require exhaustion of credit remedies first. Exclude force majeure, planned maintenance, and customer misconfiguration.
4) Operational controls: suggest instrumenting the contract with explicit monitoring dashboards, SLO measurement methods (how latency/uptime computed), weekly ops sync for 60 days post-launch, and an SLA dashboard read-only link for OmniHealth.

Risks: the buyout cap and LDs aggregate cap are the primary commercial mitigants. If the customer insists on their original ask, we should escalate to commercial leadership for approval and consider a pricing uplift to account for indemnity.

Proposed counterlanguage to offer the customer in first reply (draft to send to Alicia):
- Fee-at-risk: 10% monthly cap applied for first 6 months post-go-live, held as retention on invoices or deposited in escrow at customer election, refundable on cure or reduced after stability milestone.
- Cure & buyout: after two consecutive SLO misses, Redwood gets 30 days to remediate; if remediation fails, OmniHealth may terminate and will receive a pro-rated buyout equal to 3 months of committed fees (no larger).
- LDs: only for Redwood-caused data-integrity incidents, cap equal to 100% of committed annual fees, credits must be exhausted first.

If we go back with this, pricing should include a 7–10% uplift to compensate. Happy to draft redline language.

-Rishi
General Counsel (interim) | Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Brewer <alicia.brewer@omnihealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood counterproposal on fee-at-risk / buyout / LDs for OmniHealth

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear redline and patience while we reviewed. We discussed internally (legal + AM). Below is our proposed compromise that preserves your regulatory protections while keeping the arrangement commercially sustainable.

1) Fee-at-risk: capped at 10% of the monthly committed fee, applied for the first 6 months after go-live. The customer may elect either (a) escrow of the capped amount at signing or (b) retention on quarterly invoices. Amounts are refundable if stability milestones are met per the SLO schedule.

2) Termination & buyout: if Redwood misses the agreed 99.9% uptime SLO for two consecutive billing months, OmniHealth will provide written notice and Redwood will have 30 days to remediate. If remediation is unsuccessful and SLO misses continue materially, OmniHealth may terminate the agreement. In that case, the buyout payable to OmniHealth will be equal to 3 months of committed fees (pro-rated), not the remainder of the term.

3) Liquidated damages: for demonstrable Redwood-caused data-integrity incidents (i.e., serving/runtime defects that cause irrecoverable data corruption), LDs will be available in addition to credits but capped in the aggregate at 100% of the committed annual fee. Credits must be applied/exhausted prior to LD payout. Exclusions: force majeure, customer misconfiguration, and third-party upstream failures.

4) Operational / measurement: we will publish a read-only SLO dashboard and provide weekly ops synces for the first 60 days post-launch. SLO definitions and measurement methodology are included in the attached redline.

We believe this addresses OmniHealth’s regulatory concern while keeping the commercial exposure bounded. As Rishi mentioned, an uplift to pricing (we propose +8% on committed fees) would be standard to offset the additional commercial risk. Happy to discuss on a short call — are you available today 11:00–11:30 PT or Wednesday morning?

If this looks acceptable, we can produce a clean redline and DocuSign-ready SOW for signature.

Thanks — Neha

Neha — appreciate the fast, thoughtful counterproposal and the clarity on operational controls. Overall this moves us in the right direction. A few quick items from procurement/legal:

- We can accept 10% monthly fee-at-risk for the first 6 months if Redwood agrees to escrow (OmniHealth will initiate escrow instructions).
- The 30-day cure and 3-month buyout are acceptable as long as the remediation plan is documented and an independent post-mortem is provided for each SLO miss.
- For LDs, the 100% annual cap is acceptable so long as the contract explicitly defines "demonstrable Redwood-caused data-integrity incident" (we'll redline to narrow the definition).
- About pricing: procurement will evaluate the +8% uplift but prefers to absorb via committed term rather than increased unit rates. We'll discuss on the call.

Let's take the call tomorrow 11:00 PT to finalize language; I’ll send a calendar invite. If we can close by 6/3 we will proceed with onboarding.

Best,
Alicia
VP, IT & Cloud Operations
OmniHealth
